4) Population constraints (apply after entry):
   - Include the first qualifying event per person only (index is the person’s earliest qualifying event).
   - Include persons of all ages (no age restrictions).
   - Include all sexes (male, female, unknown) — analytic breakdown by sex will be performed later.
   - Require no minimum prior or subsequent observation time (no continuous observation window required).

5) Visit / setting:

6) Time window:
   - Use all available data in the source (no calendar start or end date restrictions). Index dates may be any date within the person’s observation period in the database.
   - Mortality outcome ascertainment window: for cohort definition, persons remain at-risk from index date until cohort exit (see Exit). Mortality will be calculated across the whole available follow-up period after index.

7) Exclusions:
   - No exclusion criteria. Do not exclude hospice, long-term care, pediatric or other subgroups.

   - Exit a person on the earliest of: date of death (death_date in OBSERVATION_PERIOD/DEATH table) OR end of the person’s observation period in the database (observation_period.end_date). influenza_roots AS (
  SELECT CAST(x AS INT64) AS concept_id
  FROM UNNEST(CAST([] AS ARRAY<INT64>)) AS x

covid_roots AS (
  SELECT CAST(x AS INT64) AS concept_id
  FROM UNNEST(CAST([] AS ARRAY<INT64>)) AS x
),
sarscov2_positive_roots AS (
  -- This set is intended to include positive/result concepts and/or SARS-CoV-2 test concept roots as curated by analysts
  SELECT CAST(x AS INT64) AS concept_id
  FROM UNNEST(CAST([] AS ARRAY<INT64>)) AS x
),
-- Expand to all descendant standard concepts (SNOMED/LOINC/measurement as appropriate)
influenza_concepts AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` ca
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` c
    ON ca.descendant_concept_id = c.concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (SELECT concept_id FROM influenza_roots)
    AND (c.standard_concept = 'S' OR c.standard_concept IS NULL) -- keep descendants; analysts should ensure roots are standard

covid_condition_concepts AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` ca
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` c
    ON ca.descendant_concept_id = c.concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (SELECT concept_id FROM covid_roots)
    AND (c.standard_concept = 'S' OR c.standard_concept IS NULL)
),

  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` ca
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` c
    ON ca.descendant_concept_id = c.concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (SELECT concept_id FROM sarscov2_positive_roots)
    AND c.domain_id = 'Measurement'
    AND (c.standard_concept = 'S' OR c.standard_concept IS NULL)
),

   AND DATE(co.condition_start_date) BETWEEN DATE(op.observation_period_start_date) AND DATE(op.observation_period_end_date)
),
-- Qualifying COVID events: positive measurements
covid_measurement_events AS (
  SELECT
    m.person_id,
    DATE(m.measurement_date) AS event_date
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.measurement` m
  LEFT JOIN sarscov2_measurement_concepts mc
    ON m.measurement_concept_id = mc.concept_id
  LEFT JOIN sarscov2_positive_result_concepts pr
    ON m.value_as_concept_id = pr.concept_id
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.observation_period` op
    ON m.person_id = op.person_id
   AND DATE(m.measurement_date) BETWEEN DATE(op.observation_period_start_date) AND DATE(op.observation_period_end_date)
  WHERE (
    -- Either the measurement is of a SARS-CoV-2 test (measurement_concept_id matched) AND result indicates positive,
    (mc.concept_id IS NOT NULL AND (pr.concept_id IS NOT NULL OR LOWER(COALESCE(m.value_as_string, '')) IN ('detected','detected by nucleic acid amplification','positive','pos','present'))) 
    -- OR the measurement result itself is coded as a positive concept (regardless of measurement_concept_id)
    OR pr.concept_id IS NOT NULL
  )
),
covid_events_union AS (
  SELECT * FROM covid_condition_events
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM covid_measurement_events
),
covid_index AS (
  SELECT person_id, MIN(event_date) AS index_date
  FROM covid_events_union
  GROUP BY person_id
),
-- Combine cohorts with cohort ids: 1 = Influenza, 2 = COVID-19
combined_indices AS (
  SELECT 1 AS cohort_definition_id, ii.person_id, ii.index_date
  FROM influenza_index ii
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 2 AS cohort_definition_id, ci.person_id, ci.index_date
  FROM covid_index ci
),
-- Attach observation_period that contains the index date to determine observation end and ensure index falls within observation
index_with_obs AS (
  SELECT
    ci.cohort_definition_id,
    ci.person_id,
    ci.index_date,
    op.observation_period_start_date,
    op.observation_period_end_date
  FROM combined_indices ci
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.observation_period` op
    ON ci.person_id = op.person_id
   AND DATE(ci.index_date) BETWEEN DATE(op.observation_period_start_date) AND DATE(op.observation_period_end_date)
),
-- Get death dates (if any)
person_death AS (
  SELECT person_id, DATE(death_date) AS death_date
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.death`
)

SELECT
  iwo.cohort_definition_id,
  iwo.person_id,
  i.index_date AS cohort_start_date,
  -- cohort end = earliest of death_date (if any) or observation_period_end_date
  CASE
    WHEN pd.death_date IS NULL THEN DATE(iwo.observation_period_end_date)
    ELSE LEAST(pd.death_date, DATE(iwo.observation_period_end_date))
  END AS cohort_end_date
FROM (
  SELECT cohort_definition_id, person_id, index_date FROM index_with_obs
) i
LEFT JOIN index_with_obs iwo
  ON i.cohort_definition_id = iwo.cohort_definition_id AND i.person_id = iwo.person_id AND i.index_date = iwo.index_date
LEFT JOIN person_death pd
  ON i.person_id = pd.person_id
ORDER BY cohort_definition_id, person_id;

Final Cohort Definition

1) Cohort structure (two separate cohorts to be implemented separately in ATLAS):
   - Cohort A: Influenza cohort
   - Cohort B: COVID-19 cohort

2) Index event (for each cohort):
   - Index date = date of first qualifying event for that person (see Entry Criteria). Use the earliest qualifying event ever in the available data (first-ever within the person’s observation history in the source data).

3) Entry criteria (qualifying events):
   - Cohort A (Influenza): any condition occurrence record where the condition_concept_id is a standard concept representing influenza (include all descendant concepts of the standard SNOMED/ICD concept(s) for influenza/influenza-like illness). A person qualifies on the date of the earliest such condition occurrence.
   - Cohort B (COVID-19): any of the following:
       a) condition occurrence record where the condition_concept_id is a standard concept representing COVID-19 / SARS-CoV-2 infection (include all descendant concepts), OR
       b) a measurement record for a SARS-CoV-2 virus test with a value indicating detected/positive (include all standard LOINC or measurement concepts for SARS-CoV-2 with result mapped to a positive/detected concept or value). A person qualifies on the date of the earliest such qualifying condition occurrence or positive measurement.

4) Population constraints (apply after entry):
   - Include the first qualifying event per person only (index is the person’s earliest qualifying event).
   - Include persons of all ages (no age restrictions).
   - Include all sexes (male, female, unknown) — analytic breakdown by sex will be performed later.
   - Require no minimum prior or subsequent observation time (no continuous observation window required).

5) Visit / setting:
   - No restriction on care setting. Qualifying events may occur in any clinical setting (inpatient, outpatient, emergency, etc.).

6) Time window:
   - Use all available data in the source (no calendar start or end date restrictions). Index dates may be any date within the person’s observation period in the database.
   - Mortality outcome ascertainment window: for cohort definition, persons remain at-risk from index date until cohort exit (see Exit). Mortality will be calculated across the whole available follow-up period after index.

7) Exclusions:
   - No exclusion criteria. Do not exclude hospice, long-term care, pediatric or other subgroups.

8) Exit (cohort end date):
   - Exit a person on the earliest of: date of death (death_date in OBSERVATION_PERIOD/DEATH table) OR end of the person’s observation period in the database (observation_period.end_date). Persons may re-enter only if a new cohort is constructed allowing multiple entries; for this definition use single entry per person (first-ever event).

9) Assumptions (explicit, conservative defaults):
   - Assumption: ‘‘All available data’’ means the entire observation period available in the source database; no calendar restrictions will be applied unless later requested.
   - Assumption: For clinical condition identification we will use standard OMOP vocabulary concepts (SNOMED for conditions, LOINC/measurement concepts for tests) and include all descendant concepts of chosen root concepts representing influenza and COVID-19; the specific concept lists will be curated prior to implementation.
   - Assumption: For COVID-19 cohort we include positive SARS-CoV-2 measurements in addition to diagnosis codes to capture cases recorded only as positive tests. For Influenza cohort we currently require condition occurrence diagnosis codes (positive influenza lab measurements may be added if requested).
   - Assumption: Index is defined as the person’s first-ever qualifying event in the available data (incident-first definition). This is conservative for mortality attribution because follow-up begins at first known diagnosis/test.
   - Assumption: No prior observation requirement is imposed; some index events may represent prevalent (existing) cases recorded at first appearance in the database.
   - Assumption: No exclusions (for hospice, long-term care, pediatrics, comorbidities) were requested — none will be applied.

Notes for implementation and analysis:
   - The cohorts defined above are intended for upstream cohort construction only. The mortality metric (numerator: deaths among cohort members; denominator: cohort size or person-time depending on chosen rate) and stratification by sex will be applied during analytic steps (not embedded in the cohort definition).
   - Prior to running, the implementing analyst must finalize and document the exact concept sets (standard concept IDs) used for ‘‘influenza’’ and ‘‘COVID-19 / SARS-CoV-2’’ and for ‘‘positive’’ measurement results, and may adapt inclusion of influenza positive measurements if desired.

End of definition.

WITH
-- Placeholder root concept lists: analysts must populate these arrays with vetted standard concept IDs from Athena
influenza_roots AS (
  SELECT CAST(x AS INT64) AS concept_id
  FROM UNNEST(CAST([] AS ARRAY<INT64>)) AS x
),
covid_roots AS (
  SELECT CAST(x AS INT64) AS concept_id
  FROM UNNEST(CAST([] AS ARRAY<INT64>)) AS x
),
sarscov2_positive_roots AS (
  -- This set is intended to include positive/result concepts and/or SARS-CoV-2 test concept roots as curated by analysts
  SELECT CAST(x AS INT64) AS concept_id
  FROM UNNEST(CAST([] AS ARRAY<INT64>)) AS x
),
-- Expand to all descendant standard concepts (SNOMED/LOINC/measurement as appropriate)
influenza_concepts AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` ca
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` c
    ON ca.descendant_concept_id = c.concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (SELECT concept_id FROM influenza_roots)
    AND (c.standard_concept = 'S' OR c.standard_concept IS NULL) -- keep descendants; analysts should ensure roots are standard
),
covid_condition_concepts AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` ca
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` c
    ON ca.descendant_concept_id = c.concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (SELECT concept_id FROM covid_roots)
    AND (c.standard_concept = 'S' OR c.standard_concept IS NULL)
),
-- Candidate measurement concepts related to SARS-CoV-2 tests (analyst should include LOINC/measurement roots in sarscov2_positive_roots if desired)
sarscov2_measurement_concepts AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` ca
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` c
    ON ca.descendant_concept_id = c.concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (SELECT concept_id FROM sarscov2_positive_roots)
    AND c.domain_id = 'Measurement'
    AND (c.standard_concept = 'S' OR c.standard_concept IS NULL)
),
-- Candidate positive/result concepts (value_as_concept_id) expanded
sarscov2_positive_result_concepts AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` ca
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` c
    ON ca.descendant_concept_id = c.concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (SELECT concept_id FROM sarscov2_positive_roots)
    AND (c.standard_concept = 'S' OR c.standard_concept IS NULL)
),
-- Qualifying influenza condition events (earliest per person)
influenza_events AS (
  SELECT
    co.person_id,
    DATE(co.condition_start_date) AS event_date
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.condition_occurrence` co
  JOIN influenza_concepts ic
    ON co.condition_concept_id = ic.concept_id
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.observation_period` op
    ON co.person_id = op.person_id
   AND DATE(co.condition_start_date) BETWEEN DATE(op.observation_period_start_date) AND DATE(op.observation_period_end_date)
),
influenza_index AS (
  SELECT person_id, MIN(event_date) AS index_date
  FROM influenza_events
  GROUP BY person_id
),
-- Qualifying COVID events: conditions
covid_condition_events AS (
  SELECT
    co.person_id,
    DATE(co.condition_start_date) AS event_date
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.condition_occurrence` co
  JOIN covid_condition_concepts cc
    ON co.condition_concept_id = cc.concept_id
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.observation_period` op
    ON co.person_id = op.person_id
   AND DATE(co.condition_start_date) BETWEEN DATE(op.observation_period_start_date) AND DATE(op.observation_period_end_date)
),
-- Qualifying COVID events: positive measurements
covid_measurement_events AS (
  SELECT
    m.person_id,
    DATE(m.measurement_date) AS event_date
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.measurement` m
  LEFT JOIN sarscov2_measurement_concepts mc
    ON m.measurement_concept_id = mc.concept_id
  LEFT JOIN sarscov2_positive_result_concepts pr
    ON m.value_as_concept_id = pr.concept_id
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.observation_period` op
    ON m.person_id = op.person_id
   AND DATE(m.measurement_date) BETWEEN DATE(op.observation_period_start_date) AND DATE(op.observation_period_end_date)
  WHERE (
    -- Either the measurement is of a SARS-CoV-2 test (measurement_concept_id matched) AND result indicates positive,
    (mc.concept_id IS NOT NULL AND (pr.concept_id IS NOT NULL OR LOWER(COALESCE(m.value_as_string, '')) IN ('detected','detected by nucleic acid amplification','positive','pos','present'))) 
    -- OR the measurement result itself is coded as a positive concept (regardless of measurement_concept_id)
    OR pr.concept_id IS NOT NULL
  )
),
covid_events_union AS (
  SELECT * FROM covid_condition_events
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM covid_measurement_events
),
covid_index AS (
  SELECT person_id, MIN(event_date) AS index_date
  FROM covid_events_union
  GROUP BY person_id
),
-- Combine cohorts with cohort ids: 1 = Influenza, 2 = COVID-19
combined_indices AS (
  SELECT 1 AS cohort_definition_id, ii.person_id, ii.index_date
  FROM influenza_index ii
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 2 AS cohort_definition_id, ci.person_id, ci.index_date
  FROM covid_index ci
),
-- Attach observation_period that contains the index date to determine observation end and ensure index falls within observation
index_with_obs AS (
  SELECT
    ci.cohort_definition_id,
    ci.person_id,
    ci.index_date,
    op.observation_period_start_date,
    op.observation_period_end_date
  FROM combined_indices ci
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.observation_period` op
    ON ci.person_id = op.person_id
   AND DATE(ci.index_date) BETWEEN DATE(op.observation_period_start_date) AND DATE(op.observation_period_end_date)
),
-- Get death dates (if any)
person_death AS (
  SELECT person_id, DATE(death_date) AS death_date
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.death`
)

SELECT
  iwo.cohort_definition_id,
  iwo.person_id,
  i.index_date AS cohort_start_date,
  -- cohort end = earliest of death_date (if any) or observation_period_end_date
  CASE
    WHEN pd.death_date IS NULL THEN DATE(iwo.observation_period_end_date)
    ELSE LEAST(pd.death_date, DATE(iwo.observation_period_end_date))
  END AS cohort_end_date
FROM (
  SELECT cohort_definition_id, person_id, index_date FROM index_with_obs
) i
LEFT JOIN index_with_obs iwo
  ON i.cohort_definition_id = iwo.cohort_definition_id AND i.person_id = iwo.person_id AND i.index_date = iwo.index_date
LEFT JOIN person_death pd
  ON i.person_id = pd.person_id
ORDER BY cohort_definition_id, person_id;

{"value": "Final Cohort Definition

1) Cohort structure (two separate cohorts to be implemented separately in ATLAS):
   - Cohort A: Influenza cohort
   - Cohort B: COVID-19 cohort

2) Index event (for each cohort):
   - Index date = date of first qualifying event for that person (see Entry Criteria). Use the earliest qualifying event ever in the available data (first-ever within the person’s observation history in the source data).

3) Entry criteria (qualifying events):
   - Cohort A (Influenza): any condition occurrence record where the condition_concept_id is a standard concept representing influenza (include all descendant concepts of the standard SNOMED/ICD concept(s) for influenza/influenza-like illness). A person qualifies on the date of the earliest such condition occurrence.
   - Cohort B (COVID-19): any of the following:
       a) condition occurrence record where the condition_concept_id is a standard concept representing COVID-19 / SARS-CoV-2 infection (include all descendant concepts), OR
       b) a measurement record for a SARS-CoV-2 virus test with a value indicating detected/positive (include all standard LOINC or measurement concepts for SARS-CoV-2 with result mapped to a positive/detected concept or value). A person qualifies on the date of the earliest such qualifying condition occurrence or positive measurement.

4) Population constraints (apply after entry):
   - Include the first qualifying event per person only (index is the person’s earliest qualifying event).
   - Include persons of all ages (no age restrictions).
   - Include all sexes (male, female, unknown) — analytic breakdown by sex will be performed later.
   - Require no minimum prior or subsequent observation time (no continuous observation window required).

5) Visit / setting:
   - No restriction on care setting. Qualifying events may occur in any clinical setting (inpatient, outpatient, emergency, etc.).

6) Time window:
   - Use all available data in the source (no calendar start or end date restrictions). Index dates may be any date within the person’s observation period in the database.
   - Mortality outcome ascertainment window: for cohort definition, persons remain at-risk from index date until cohort exit (see Exit). Mortality will be calculated across the whole available follow-up period after index.

7) Exclusions:
   - No exclusion criteria. Do not exclude hospice, long-term care, pediatric or other subgroups.

8) Exit (cohort end date):
   - Exit a person on the earliest of: date of death (death_date in OBSERVATION_PERIOD/DEATH table) OR end of the person’s observation period in the database (observation_period.end_date). Persons may re-enter only if a new cohort is constructed allowing multiple entries; for this definition use single entry per person (first-ever event).

9) Assumptions (explicit, conservative defaults):
   - Assumption: ‘‘All available data’’ means the entire observation period available in the source database; no calendar restrictions will be applied unless later requested.
   - Assumption: For clinical condition identification we will use standard OMOP vocabulary concepts (SNOMED for conditions, LOINC/measurement concepts for tests) and include all descendant concepts of chosen root concepts representing influenza and COVID-19; the specific concept lists will be curated prior to implementation.
   - Assumption: For COVID-19 cohort we include positive SARS-CoV-2 measurements in addition to diagnosis codes to capture cases recorded only as positive tests. For Influenza cohort we currently require condition occurrence diagnosis codes (positive influenza lab measurements may be added if requested).
   - Assumption: Index is defined as the person’s first-ever qualifying event in the available data (incident-first definition). This is conservative for mortality attribution because follow-up begins at first known diagnosis/test.
   - Assumption: No prior observation requirement is imposed; some index events may represent prevalent (existing) cases recorded at first appearance in the database.
   - Assumption: No exclusions (for hospice, long-term care, pediatrics, comorbidities) were requested — none will be applied.

Notes for implementation and analysis:
   - The cohorts defined above are intended for upstream cohort construction only. The mortality metric (numerator: deaths among cohort members; denominator: cohort size or person-time depending on chosen rate) and stratification by sex will be applied during analytic steps (not embedded in the cohort definition).
   - Prior to running, the implementing analyst must finalize and document the exact concept sets (standard concept IDs) used for ‘‘influenza’’ and ‘‘COVID-19 / SARS-CoV-2’’ and for ‘‘positive’’ measurement results, and may adapt inclusion of influenza positive measurements if desired.

End of definition."}
